子弟 are sons and younger brothers; the idiomatic dropped the junior kinsmen who brought the news.

東幸 is an imperial progress, not a campaign, but the proposed wording still makes the conscripts the visitors; the edict orders the repairs and plans the emperor’s eastern visit.

太子少詹事 is the junior director of the heir’s household, not junior grand mentor; 遷右庶子 is the following transfer.

He served successively as Junior Supervisor of the Household of the Heir Apparent and was transferred to Right Vice Director of the Heir Apparent's Household.
The same 少詹事 error appears in the literal field and is correctly replaced as junior supervisor of the heir apparent’s household.

The Duke of Zhou was endowed with sagehood, yet he attended others in the bath and shared his meal with humble scholars from thatched cottages—how much more should you, who stand below the Duke of Zhou?

The Duke of Zhou was endowed with sagehood, yet he would pause mid-wash and spit out his food to receive guests, and he went down to men in thatched cottages—how much more should those below the Duke of Zhou do so?

握沐吐飧 is the topos of interrupting wash and meal to receive worthies, and 下白屋 is condescending to men in humble cottages; the original bath-attendance reading is false, and 下周公之人 is generic, not a direct 'you.'
Soon he was recalled and appointed governor of Chaozhou, then transferred to Dengzhou, and never again allowed near the heir.
Soon he was recalled and appointed governor of Chaozhou, then transferred to Dengzhou, and to the end was never again kept in close confidence.
訖不復親近 says he was never again kept in intimacy; it does not name the heir, whom the original English invents.
